title: Hello, World!
lesson:
## Print & Output

The `print()` function is your primary way to display output in Python.

### Basic Usage
```python
print("Hello, World!")  # prints a string
print(42)               # prints a number
print(3.14)             # prints a float
```

### Multiple Arguments
You can pass multiple values separated by commas:
```python
print("Name:", "Alice")   # Name: Alice
print(1, 2, 3)             # 1 2 3
```

### The `sep` Parameter
Controls what goes between multiple arguments (default is a space):
```python
print("a", "b", "c", sep="-")   # a-b-c
print("a", "b", "c", sep="")    # abc
```

### The `end` Parameter
Controls what is printed at the end (default is a newline `\n`):
```python
print("Hello", end=" ")
print("World")  # Hello World  (on same line)
```

### String Types
```python
print('single quotes')   # works fine
print("double quotes")   # also works
print("She said \"hi\"")  # escaped quotes
```

Print `Hello, World!` exactly.

**Expected output:**
